Subject: Re: Intro + POC scope — quick recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the context on Acme's evaluation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up any capacity: 

1) Success criteria (what will make the POC a go):
- Latency: 95th percentile sub-150ms for single-turn chat at 2k concurrent users equivalent (simulated load).
- Cost: token cost not to exceed $0.0008 per generated token on average across typical queries.
- Feature: support function/tool calling with structured JSON outputs and streaming enabled.
- Reliability: no more than 1% request error rate over 48-hour load test.

2) Evaluation plan & timelines:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and sign SOW/ordering document.
- Week 1: Dedicated POC environment provisioned, reserved capacity + autoscaling policies configured.
- Week 2: Integration + test prompts, small-scale smoke tests.
- Week 3: Full load run + regression checks, cost/runbook handoff.

3) Capacity ask for planning:
- Baseline reserved: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) for steady-state testing.
- Autoscaling: burst to 12 GPUs for short spikes (up to 10 minutes) during ramp tests.
- KV cache and batching config to be tuned based on sample prompt distribution.

4) Ownership / actions: 
- Acme: provide sample production traffic/profile and the list of “top 200” prompt templates (Daniel + Priya).
- Redwood: provide capacity worksheet + formal proposal (Marissa), config recommendations (David + Rishi).

I attached a quick capacity worksheet and the draft proposal for your review. If this looks right, can we target signature on the SOW by EOD Thursday so we can start provisioning early next week?

Thanks,

Thanks Daniel — good questions. Quick answers and a bit more detail on the burst/autoscale behavior: 

- Burst window: Reserved capacity (4 GPUs) is guaranteed for the POC. We support short bursts above reserved capacity for up to 15 minutes without requiring manual approval — that is handled by the autoscaling policy (burst pool). For sustained usage beyond 15 minutes, autoscaling will attempt to provision additional capacity from the customer's burst quota or fall back to best-effort spot capacity which may introduce queueing.
- Cold start: For a cold-starting model container the median additional latency is ~120ms on A100-class hosts for the models we typically recommend. We recommend pre-warming during ramp tests to remove this variable.
- Tool-calling variance: We'll document the expected latency delta for each model variant in the SOW appendix.

David and Rishi, tagging you for config notes below — can you confirm the suggested autoscaling policy and KV cache sizing based on Acme's sample distribution once they send it?

Marissa

Subject: Re: POC capacity planning — autoscale + config recommendations

Great thread — calling out concrete config recommendations for the POC based on Marissa's baseline and Daniel's traffic notes: 

1) Reserved capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state). Use pinned model variant: redwood-open-7b-v2-quant (recommended for cost/latency balance).
2) Burst/autoscale policy:
   - Min: 4 GPUs (reserved)
   - Max Burst: 12 GPUs (burst pool) with 15-minute sustained threshold before fall-through to spot
   - Scale step: +2 GPUs per 30s evaluation window (smooth ramp)
   - Pre-warm: spin up 2 containers 5 minutes before scheduled full-load run to reduce cold-starts
3) KV cache sizing: allocate 20GB per GPU based on 95th percentile prompt length and expected session stickiness — this should keep most sessions cache-hit for single-turn flows.
4) Batching policy: dynamic batching with a 10ms window for user-facing, 50ms for the synthetic load runner to prioritize throughput.

Operational notes:
- We'll enable request-level tracing and sampling (10%) during the POC so we can correlate latency spikes to model/container events.
- Monica (CS) will lead run logistics; she'll coordinate the scheduled full-load window and post-run analysis with Acme.

I'll update the capacity worksheet and push a revised sheet to the shared Drive link.
